content.text:
I have what I need; here is the assessment.

**Short answer: removing it is easier, and neither option adds any upstream footprint.**

The top bar on Home is the fork's own StatusRow, a wxPanel the ShellController inserts at the top of MainFrame's main sizer once at install time ([ShellController.cpp:250](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:250)). It is not an OrcaSlicer widget. The Home page itself is a separate fork-owned WebView that swaps places with the Notebook in the workspace slot, so nothing about Home's chrome touches upstream code. Both options are edits to two fork files only, ShellController.cpp and possibly StatusRow.cpp, and MainFrame.cpp keeps its single existing attachment line either way.

**Option A, remove the bar on Home (about 5 lines).** The page-change handler at [ShellController.cpp:492](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:492) already computes whether Home is selected and shows or hides the Home view and the Notebook. Adding a `m_status_row->Show(!home)` plus a `m_main_sizer->Layout()` there finishes the job. Two things to verify when doing it:

- Home has no Back or Home button of its own, so leaving Home has to happen through the page's own actions. That is already the case today since the bar's Home button is meaningless on Home, but I have not confirmed every route off Home lives in the page.
- On macOS the frame is a normal titled window, so hiding the bar does not expose traffic-light overlap. I would still run it to see the layout jump when the bar collapses.

**Option B, blank bar with a centered logo (roughly 40 to 80 lines).** Same toggle as above, plus a second small fork panel that paints the mark from `resources/jusprin/branding/jusprin-mark.svg` through ShellTheme, and the same show/hide swap between StatusRow and the logo panel. Nothing in StatusRow today knows how to draw the brand mark, and the SVG is not yet loaded anywhere in the shell, so that loading path is new code. It also needs a design-system token for the bar height and logo size so the design-system rule about no literals holds.

Neither option is much work, but Option A is a single conditional inside code that already exists. Option B is the one to pick only if the design wants a visible brand mark or a consistent bar height across screens.

Upstream footprint for both is zero. Every changed line lives under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, and the one MainFrame line the fork already owns does not change. Rebase risk is unchanged.

One caveat I did not verify: the Home web page's own gallery header, which sits inside the WebView, may already carry a title. If it does, a native logo bar above it would double up the branding, and that would be one more reason to just remove the bar.
Just remove it. make sure you remove all the code so that you don't leave dead code behind. also you can directly commit to jusprin-newui branch
I'll read the StatusRow implementation first to find what becomes dead once the bar is never shown on Home, then check where the jusprin-newui branch is checked out.

---
name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints "interrupted by user", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

content.text:
Done. The Home screen no longer shows the project header. The change is committed directly on jusprin-newui as `42f14d7005` ("Hide the project header on Home"), and the shell harness passes with zero failures on the fresh build.

**What changed**

- [ShellController.cpp:512](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:512) hides the header whenever the Notebook's selection is Home and shows it again on the way back. This happens in the same handler that already swaps Home for the Notebook and collapses the Agent pane, so there is no new state.
- StatusRow lost the code that only existed because the header used to be visible on Home. The Home button always navigates to Home now instead of toggling, its label no longer flips to "Prepare", and the tab-change subscription that refreshed that label is removed along with its handler and bind/unbind pair.
- The shell harness now asserts the header is hidden on Home at startup and on every return, and shown on Prepare. The header layout checks moved to the first arrival on Prepare, where the row is actually laid out. Navigation steps leave Home through the same request the Home page's backend uses.

**Upstream footprint** is zero. Every changed line is under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` or `tests/shell/`. The single MainFrame attachment line is untouched.

**Verification** was a full RelWithDebInfo rebuild of the app and `shell_integration_harness` in the main checkout, followed by the harness's default mode with a fresh scratch home. All checks passed, including the new ones and the resize checks that exercise the header on Prepare.

One side effect to know about: I reconfigured the main checkout's build with tests enabled so the harness could be built there. That does not change the app build, but the next incremental build in that directory now also generates the test targets. The session worktree was fast-forwarded to the same commit and is clean.
